weeks.title: The /dʒ/ sound spelt ge and dge at the end of words, and sometimes g before e, i, y

routine.Warm up: Revisit Year 1 suffix spellings (-s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est) with a quick oral spell of two or three words.
routine.Teach the pattern: The letter "j" is never used for this sound at the end of an English word. Straight after a short vowel sound, it is spelt -dge; after any other sound it is spelt -ge. Inside a word, this sound is often (not always) spelt g before e, i or y. Example words: badge, edge, bridge, dodge, fudge, age.
routine.Have a go: Children spell a short set of this week's example words on mini-whiteboards, checking each one against the pattern just taught.
routine.Use it: Children write a dictated sentence built from this week's words (see dictation bank), then check it reads back correctly.

dictation: The dog sat by the bridge.
She felt the huge change in the village.
The giant read by magic light.
He put his jacket on to jog to the bridge.

weeks.title: The /s/ sound spelt c before e, i, y

routine.Warm up: Revisit last week's pattern with a quick oral spell of two or three of its words.
routine.Teach the pattern: A "c" says /s/ specifically when it comes before e, i or y. Example words: race, ice, cell, city, fancy.
routine.Have a go: Children spell a short set of this week's example words on mini-whiteboards, checking each one against the pattern just taught.
routine.Use it: Children write a dictated sentence built from this week's words (see dictation bank), then check it reads back correctly.

dictation: The city had a fancy race.
The cold ice melted near the cell door.

weeks.title: The /n/ sound spelt kn and (less often) gn at the beginning of words

routine.Warm up: Revisit last week's pattern with a quick oral spell of two or three of its words.
routine.Teach the pattern: The "k" and "g" were pronounced hundreds of years ago and are now silent. Example words: knock, know, knee, gnat, gnaw.
routine.Have a go: Children spell a short set of this week's example words on mini-whiteboards, checking each one against the pattern just taught.
routine.Use it: Children write a dictated sentence built from this week's words (see dictation bank), then check it reads back correctly.

dictation: I know that is her knee.
The gnat sat on the gnarled branch.

weeks.title: The /r/ sound spelt wr at the beginning of words

routine.Warm up: Revisit last week's pattern with a quick oral spell of two or three of its words.
routine.Teach the pattern: Also reflects an old pronunciation — the "w" is silent. Example words: write, written, wrote, wrong, wrap.
routine.Have a go: Children spell a short set of this week's example words on mini-whiteboards, checking each one against the pattern just taught.
routine.Use it: Children write a dictated sentence built from this week's words (see dictation bank), then check it reads back correctly.

dictation: She had to write it again.
She wrote that the answer was wrong.

weeks.title: Common exception words

routine.Warm up: Flash through any common exception words already met this half-term.
routine.Teach the pattern: This half-term's new common exception words: door, floor, poor, because, find, kind, mind, behind, child, children, wild. Read each one together, name the "tricky" part, then practise spelling it from memory (read-then-spell, same convention as the main phonics programme).
routine.Have a go: Children spell a selection of this half-term's common exception words on mini-whiteboards.
routine.Use it: Children write a dictated sentence using two or three of this half-term's common exception words.

dictation: The child could not find the door.
Be kind to the wild bird because it is poor.

routine.Warm up: Quick oral revisit of every pattern taught this half-term.
routine.Teach the pattern: No new content — this week consolidates everything taught so far this half-term.
routine.Have a go: Mixed practice drawing on every rule taught this half-term, not only the most recent one.
routine.Use it: The half-term spelling test (see the Year 2 spelling tests sheet) — a mix of pattern words and common exception words.
